## Security verdict: PASS

PR #226 at **0379588ac951e565c287f2b885365c35749755e3**, under C33/C34. Reviewed the five-file delta and directly relevant governance/authentication paths.

`READ_LEAVES` uses exact tuple membership for only `project list/show`, `stream list/show`, `fence show`, `node show`, and `spine events/render` (`crates/daemon/src/http/governance.rs:708-768`). `read()` implements only these eight, and `execute()` delegates to it. Listed reads preserve existing projections and do not reach writers; spine publishing remains separate (`724-756,1525-1643,1682-1734`).

Route/family agreement and parsing precede the callerless shortcut. Unknown verbs/flags, duplicate flags, aliases or prefixes do not expand it into writes. Both `--actor value` and `--actor=value`, including blank actor values, require caller resolution. A caller-bearing read retains the previous caller/actor checks (`governance.rs:385-607`).

`has_caller()` and resolution use matching nonblank checks and existing wire aliases. Missing-caller refusals have HTTP 400, `details.code: E-RS-NO-CALLER`, and the documented message prefix (`http/identity.rs:67-86,1209-1270`).

Bearer authentication still gates governance. Peer keys remain refused, and job-token authentication remains confined to background emission (`http/mod.rs:425-449,479-512,714-789`). Actorless reads return nothing beyond existing local-key-seat reads; this is C33's user-account boundary, not a new unauthenticated or federation read surface.
